answer: Because the willow index resolves every citation against the jade checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the falcon audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 175 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 175 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 23 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
